appearance_facts.fact: Title text 'Risk Index of Hazard H in US States'.
Choropleth map of US states with state abbreviation labels inside each polygon.
Vertical color legend bar with tick marks and labels 'High' at top and 'Low' at bottom.
Gradient runs from pale yellow at top (100) through orange to dark maroon at bottom (0).
New Mexico (NM) polygon is filled with the darkest maroon color, matching the bottom of the legend.
Rhode Island (RI) polygon is filled with pale yellow, matching the top of the legend.
Delaware (DE) polygon is filled with a light orange/peach color, mid-range on the legend.

appearance_facts.location: Various states (WA, ID, WY, KS, OK, VT, NH, NY, NJ)
appearance_facts.fact: Several states share the same dark maroon fill as NM, indicating similarly low index values.

public_definitions: Routing criterion: Highest risk state in the dashboard
Record workflow: State risk priority follow-up
User goal: open the state risk record that should be routed into the highest-risk priority follow-up workflow
uncertain: The legend direction is ambiguous: 'High' is at the top (100, pale yellow) and 'Low' is at the bottom (0, dark maroon), but typically higher risk is associated with darker/warmer colors. The visual encoding here inverts the standard convention where dark=high.
Exact numerical values for each state are not provided; only the color scale is available.

Whether 'highest risk' corresponds to the highest index value (100, pale yellow) or the lowest index value (0, dark maroon) depends on the definition of 'Risk Index' which is not explicitly stated beyond the title.
